claim: The level of the `rejection` line is never asserted: written at info instead of warning, for every cause (401 without a token, 401 refused token, 403 missing scope, 503 no signing keys), no test notices, although the level of every other event is pinned by a test.
evidence: Mutant enterich.app.x__log_rejection__mutmut_19 drops logging.WARNING at src/enterich/app.py:227, so log.event falls back to logging.INFO (src/enterich/log.py:59) and the line's `level` becomes "info". Checked by running the service: the original writes level "warning" for all four causes. Every rejection assertion compares only status, reason, sub and client: tests/integration/test_service.py:167-169, 202-204, 225-228, 248-250, 274, 418-420; tests/e2e and tests/repo have no rejection or level check. The other events' levels are all asserted: start info/warning (tests/unit/test_main.py:46, 77), operation info/warning on a refusal (tests/unit/test_tools.py:146-147), jwks info/warning on a failed fetch (tests/unit/test_auth.py:369-370), error (tests/unit/test_log.py:93, tests/unit/test_main.py:26). No spec states the value: REQ-002-PRS-NF008 names `level` as a field of every line without a level per event, so the requirement is null and this rests on the code's own contract (a refusal is a warning, as for operation and jwks). The run 2026-11-12-tests-2 refuted this same finding as unspecified (harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2/findings.jsonl); since then that run's level tests for jwks, operation, error and start were merged, and the operator's sample judged the start-level test "wanted" (sample.jsonl, d467afc), which leaves rejection as the only event whose level is unpinned.
proposal: In tests/integration/test_service.py, add the line's level to the tuples already compared: `(r["level"], r["status"], r["reason"]) == ("warning", 401, "no bearer token")` in test_missing_token_gets_401_with_the_metadata_pointer, and likewise "warning" in test_a_missing_scope_gets_403 and test_unreachable_jwks_gets_503_not_401 (and `first["level"] == "warning"` in test_a_refused_token_gets_401_and_one_short_line_each). Any one of them is red on the mutant; all causes go through _log_rejection.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute this finding; it holds, and a test alone closes it.

**The mutant.** `mutmut show enterich.app.x__log_rejection__mutmut_19` reports it as survived. It changes src/enterich/app.py:227 from `log.event("rejection", logging.WARNING, **fields)` to `log.event("rejection", **fields)`. `log.event` then defaults to `logging.INFO` (src/enterich/log.py:59), so the line's `level` is "info" instead of "warning". It is not equivalent: the line is still written (the Enterich logger is set to DEBUG, src/enterich/log.py:53), but with a different `level` value on stdout. All four causes go through `_log_rejection` (src/enterich/app.py:161, 179, 181, 188).

**No test asserts it.** I searched all of tests/ (unit, integration, e2e, repo, conftest).
- Every rejection assertion compares only status, reason, sub and client: tests/integration/test_service.py:167-169, 202-204, 225-228, 248-250, 274, 418-420.
- tests/e2e and tests/repo have no rejection or level check.
- The `logs` fixture (tests/conftest.py:59-68) checks only JSON, known events and secrets.
- tests/unit/test_log.py:55 and tests/unit/test_main.py:92 pass `logging.WARNING` to `log.event` themselves, so they never reach app.py.

**The other events' levels are pinned.** start at tests/unit/test_main.py:46 and :77, operation at tests/unit/test_tools.py:146-147, jwks at tests/unit/test_auth.py:369-370, error at tests/unit/test_log.py:93 and tests/unit/test_main.py:26. Rejection is the only Enterich event left without one.

**Observable, though not stated per event.** REQ-002-PRS-NF008 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:207-209) gives every line a `level` field but names no value per event, and REQ-002-PRS-NF009 (:231-241) names no level either. So the requirement is rightly null, and this rests on the code's own contract, which the survey rubric counts as a gap (.claude/workflows/improve-tests.js:106).

**Why I differ from the earlier refutal.** Run 2026-11-12-tests-2 refuted this same finding as unspecified (findings.jsonl:73). The same run confirmed the equally unspecified operation level as a fix with a null requirement (findings.jsonl:148). That test (73bd133) is on main, as are the jwks, error and start level tests (76cb7c7, c2764fc, ad0a274, d467afc). The operator's sample judged c2764fc and d467afc "wanted" (sample.jsonl). harness/suppressions.jsonl is empty.

**Red check.** In scratch copies of src and tests (under the session scratchpad, probe/orig and probe/mut) I added the proposed "warning" to the four tests: test_missing_token_gets_401_with_the_metadata_pointer, test_a_missing_scope_gets_403, test_a_refused_token_gets_401_and_one_short_line_each and test_unreachable_jwks_gets_503_not_401. On the original code, 4 passed. With the mutation applied, 4 failed, for example `('info', 503, 'no signing keys') != ('warning', 503, 'no signing keys')`.

**Class and pattern.** Fix: adding `level` to the tuples already compared in tests/integration/test_service.py is enough, with no code, spec or ADR change. No pattern fits. dropped-argument is about arguments sent to ERPNext, and this one goes to the logger.

I changed nothing in the repository.

claim: Nothing checks that create_app sets AuthSettings.validate_token_resource explicitly, as ADR-003 decides: set to None or left out, the SDK raises an MCPDeprecationWarning at every start (plain text on stderr) and Enterich relies on the SDK's changing default, and no test notices.
evidence: Mutants enterich.app.x_create_app__mutmut_49 (validate_token_resource=None) and enterich.app.x_create_app__mutmut_53 (argument removed) at src/enterich/app.py:55. docs/arc42/adr/ADR-003-local-token-check.md, Decision: "Enterich sets `AuthSettings.validate_token_resource` explicitly instead of relying on its changing default, because the verifier checks `aud` itself." The pinned SDK warns when it is unset and resource_server_url is set (.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/mcp/server/auth/settings.py:57-70; "it will default to True in 3.0"), and MCPDeprecationWarning is a UserWarning, shown by default (mcp/shared/exceptions.py:8). Checked outside the repository: AuthSettings with the flag None or omitted emits the warning, with False or True none; create_app(settings(), jwks.client()) and a tools/list request run clean under warnings.simplefilter("error") on the original. No test records or forbids warnings: no catch_warnings, pytest.warns, recwarn or filterwarnings in tests/, pyproject.toml ([tool.pytest] has only --strict-markers), the Dockerfile's test CMD or .github/workflows/ci.yml, so the mutants pass with only pytest's warnings summary. No spec states this (REQ-002-PRS-NF008 covers the JSON log on stdout), so the requirement is null; the source is ADR-003. Not part of this finding: enterich.app.x_create_app__mutmut_55 (True) is equivalent, because the Verifier always hands the SDK resource=settings.resource_url (src/enterich/auth.py:233), which the SDK's check (mcp/server/auth/middleware/bearer_auth.py:73-88) then always accepts.
proposal: In tests/integration/test_service.py, a test that builds the app with warnings as errors, citing ADR-003: `with warnings.catch_warnings(): warnings.simplefilter("error"); create_app(settings(), jwks.client())` (optionally followed by one tools/list request with a valid token inside the same block). It passes on the original and raises MCPDeprecationWarning on both mutants.

verdict.reason:
Could not refute; both mutants are real, observable and unguarded.

What the code and the ADR say: src/enterich/app.py:55 passes validate_token_resource=False with the comment "The verifier checks `aud` itself (ADR-003)"; docs/arc42/adr/ADR-003-local-token-check.md:23 decides "Enterich sets `AuthSettings.validate_token_resource` explicitly instead of relying on its changing default". mutmut show confirms mutmut_49 (=None) and mutmut_53 (argument removed), both "survived".

Not equivalent: the SDK's validator warns when the flag is None and resource_server_url is set (.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/mcp/server/auth/settings.py:57-70), and MCPDeprecationWarning is a UserWarning, shown by default (mcp/shared/exceptions.py:8). The HTTP behaviour is the same as False (mcp/server/mcpserver/server.py:1201-1202 hands the middleware the resource URL only when the flag is truthy), so the warning is the whole difference, but it is observable outside pytest: I ran __main__.main() (uvicorn.run replaced) on scratch copies of src/ with each mutant applied, under default warning filters. Original: stderr empty, one JSON start line on stdout. Each mutant: two plain-text MCPDeprecationWarning blocks on stderr at every start (one from app.py:50, one from the SDK re-validating its Settings at mcpserver/server.py:188). The Dockerfile sets no PYTHONWARNINGS and src/ has no captureWarnings, so the image would print them too.

No test asserts it: grep over tests/ (unit, integration, e2e, repo), pyproject.toml, Dockerfile, .github/ and harness/ finds no catch_warnings, pytest.warns, recwarn, filterwarnings, simplefilter, -W or PYTHONWARNINGS; [tool.pytest] has only --strict-markers (pyproject.toml:60-62). tests/unit/test_main.py reads only capsys .out, and pytest records warnings rather than printing them. tests/e2e builds the app in-process through the same client() helper (tests/e2e/conftest.py:52-54), so it cannot see it either. Running tests/unit and tests/integration against the mutmut_49 copy: 1090 passed, 1420 warnings.

The proposed test works: a throwaway test outside the repository (warnings.catch_warnings + simplefilter("error") around create_app(settings(), jwks.client()), and a second one adding a tools/list request with a valid token) passes on the original and raises MCPDeprecationWarning on mutmut_49 and mutmut_53; it also passes on mutmut_55 (True), consistent with the finding's claim that that one is equivalent (src/enterich/auth.py:233 always hands the SDK resource=settings.resource_url).

Class fix: a test alone closes it, within ADR-003 as it stands; no code, spec, ADR or pyproject.toml change is needed (a pytest-wide filterwarnings=error would be a pyproject.toml change and so a proposal, but the finding does not need it). Low severity, but cheap and it guards a decision an ADR records. The fix should consider narrowing the filter to MCPDeprecationWarning if a blanket "error" proves brittle on dependency updates.

Test file: tests/integration/test_service.py is the only test module that calls create_app directly (lines 295, 310, 362, 375, 394) and already cites an ADR (line 98); tests/unit/test_app.py covers only Wrapper.

Pattern null: mutmut_53 drops an argument, but to the MCP SDK's AuthSettings, not to ERPNext, which is what dropped-argument names; the other three don't apply.

Repository left unchanged (git status shows only the run directory that was already untracked); scratch copies are under /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ubuntu-dev-enterich/0431a6bc-d8e6-4381-9c7d-b9072faa4363/scratchpad/vtr.

claim: No test checks that ERPNext calls carry `Accept: application/json`, so the header can be dropped or garbled unnoticed.
evidence: src/enterich/erpnext.py:87 sets it as one of four fixed headers. tests/unit/test_erpnext.py::test_every_call_carries_the_agent_key_the_host_and_english (line 39) asserts authorization, host and accept-language only, and tests/fakes/erpnext.py never reads Accept. Under mutmut_20 the fake receives the library default `accept: */*`; mutmut_22 sends `XXapplication/jsonXX`; mutmut_23 sends `APPLICATION/JSON` (case only, but the same assertion kills it). Checked on scratch copies of the module: an assertion on the received header passes on the original and fails on all three. No spec names the header: REQ-002-PRS-NF006 lists Authorization, Host and Accept-Language. It is the code's own contract, and the refusal text of REQ-001-PRS-F008 is read from ERPNext's JSON error body, which this header asks for. Whether ERPNext v16 answers differently without it was not checked here. The sibling mutmut_21 (`ACCEPT`) is equivalent, since header names are case-insensitive.
proposal: In tests/unit/test_erpnext.py, add `assert received.headers["accept"] == "application/json"` to the loop in test_every_call_carries_the_agent_key_the_host_and_english, or add a test beside it that asserts it for one read and one write.

verdict.reason:
Refuted as not required: the finding's facts hold, but the header changes nothing ERPNext v16 answers and no spec names it. This is the check the finding left open ("Whether ERPNext v16 answers differently without it was not checked here").

What holds:
- src/enterich/erpnext.py:87 sets `"accept": "application/json"` as one of four fixed client headers.
- No test asserts it. tests/unit/test_erpnext.py:46-49 and the integration fixture's teardown at tests/integration/conftest.py:27-31 check authorization, host, accept-language and no cookie only. tests/fakes/erpnext.py:385 stores the headers but never reads Accept. tests/e2e never looks at request headers; the only other `accept` in tests/ is the MCP client's own header (tests/integration/mcp.py:20).
- `mutmut show` lists _20, _22 and _23 as survived, with the diffs the finding gives.
- A throwaway test on scratch copies (the existing loop plus `received.headers["accept"] == "application/json"`) passes on the original and fails on _20 (`*/*`), _22 (`XXapplication/jsonXX`) and _23 (`APPLICATION/JSON`). It passes on _21, which is equivalent.

Why it is refuted:
- No spec or architecture text requires the header. REQ-002-PRS-NF006 (docs/specs/req-002-service.md:179 and :185) lists what every request carries: Authorization, the configured Host, `Accept-Language: en` and no cookie. docs/arc42/README.md:71 and :115 list the same three headers.
- ERPNext v16 does not answer differently. I read Frappe's source (branch version-16, tag v16.0.0 and version-15, from raw.githubusercontent.com). The only server-side reader of the request's Accept header on the paths Enterich calls is `handle_exception`, frappe/app.py:364-367 on version-16:
  `respond_as_json = (Accept and (is_ajax or "application/json" in accept_header)) or (request.path.startswith("/api/") and not accept_header.startswith("text"))`
- Every Enterich call goes to `/api/resource/...` or `/api/method/...` (erpnext.py:122, :131, :187, :255). So errors come back as JSON under all three mutants: `*/*` and `APPLICATION/JSON` through the path clause, `XXapplication/jsonXX` through the substring clause.
- Success answers are not negotiated on Accept at all. The other match in the tree, frappe/mcp/transport.py:41, is Frappe's own MCP endpoint, which Enterich doesn't call.
- So the REQ-001-PRS-F008 refusal text (exc_type, `_server_messages`) is unaffected, and the end-to-end suite could not tell the mutants apart either.

The header is a defensive convention, and a test would only pin a constant that nothing in the contract or in v16's behaviour depends on. This matches the earlier refutations of the rejection line's level and the `rows_of` fallback in harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2/findings.jsonl.

Not checked: I did not run the end-to-end site (it isn't up) and did not search the ERPNext app's own code; the v16 conclusion rests on Frappe's source.

If triage wants it pinned anyway, the whole fix is one assertion in the loop of tests/unit/test_erpnext.py::test_every_call_carries_the_agent_key_the_host_and_english. Making the header a requirement would mean adding it to REQ-002-PRS-NF006, which I don't think is warranted.

claim: The refusal of a list that lacks exactly three fields is untested, so it can read "a, b, c and 0 more".
evidence: The count is added by `len(missing) > 3` at src/enterich/erpnext.py:285. tests/unit/test_erpnext.py covers four missing fields (test_a_list_without_a_field_asked_for_is_refused, "and 1 more") and one (test_a_list_without_a_field_above_the_users_permission_level_is_refused), never three. On a scratch copy with `>= 3` the message was "ERPNext's Item list lacks fields Enterich asked for (item_code, item_group, stock_uom and 0 more): ...". The spec's own wording (name the DocType and the read right) is still met by the mutant; the list of names and the count are the code's contract. The existing unit test marks this message as REQ-001-PRS-F018, and the same kind of boundary is pinned for the duplicates refusal at 1, 5 and 6 in tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py::test_a_refusal_names_up_to_five_drafts_and_counts_the_rest.
proposal: Add a test in tests/unit/test_erpnext.py: answer /api/resource/Item with {"data": [{"name": "SKU-1"}]}, call get_list with fields name, item_code, item_group, stock_uom, and assert the text contains "(item_code, item_group, stock_uom): the agent user". Alternatively parametrize the existing exact-text test over three and four missing fields.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed; could not refute. The mutant (`uv run --group harness mutmut show enterich.erpnext.x__check_fields__mutmut_17`) turns `len(missing) > 3` into `>= 3` at src/enterich/erpnext.py:285, and it is not equivalent: with exactly three missing fields the refusal reads "(a, b, c and 0 more)".

Checked on a scratch copy of src/ and tests/ with the mutant applied (repository untouched):
- All 1090 tests in tests/unit and tests/integration pass on the mutant.
- A throwaway test (answer /api/resource/Item with {"data": [{"name": "SKU-1"}]}, get_list with name, item_code, item_group, stock_uom, assert "(item_code, item_group, stock_uom): the agent user" in the text) fails on the mutant with "ERPNext's Item list lacks fields Enterich asked for (item_code, item_group, stock_uom and 0 more): ..." and passes on the original.

No existing test asserts it:
- tests/unit/test_erpnext.py:324-341 pins the exact text only for four missing fields ("and 1 more").
- tests/unit/test_erpnext.py:344-357 covers one missing field.
- tests/e2e/test_rights.py:97-101 matches only the start of the message ("^ERPNext's \w[\w ]* list lacks fields Enterich asked for ").
- "lacks fields" appears nowhere else under tests/.

The boundary is reached on real paths, not only in theory. A probe showed two integration tests already produce exactly three missing fields, but they check only substrings, so "and 0 more" passes:
- tests/integration/test_record_to_report.py:686-693 (Fiscal Year: year_start_date, year_end_date, companies.company) asserts "Fiscal Year" and "year_end_date" in the text.
- tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:392-403 (Sales Invoice duplicate check: items.item_code, items.qty, items.is_free_item) asserts "Sales Invoice" and "items.item_code" in the text.
So with select only on Fiscal Year or Sales Invoice, the mutant would tell the agent "... and 0 more".

Observable and within the current specs: the text reaches the agent as a tool error (REQ-001-PRS-F008, docs/specs/req-001-core.md:296). REQ-001-PRS-F018 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:439-441) requires only naming the DocType and the read right, so the names and the count are the code's own contract. The unit test already pins that contract under REQ-001-PRS-F018, and the same kind of cap is pinned at 1, 5 and 6 for the duplicates refusal (tests/integration/test_order_to_cash_drafts.py:336-350). No spec, ADR or code change is needed: class fix, test only.

Pattern limit-not-at-boundary: the three-name cap is tested one beyond (four) and well below (one), never at three. The fit is on "never at it"; the "well past" half of the definition does not apply, since four is only one beyond.

Fix location: tests/unit/test_erpnext.py, either a new three-field test or the exact-text test at line 324 parametrized over three and four missing fields. The existing `fake.fail(path, 200, body)` helper suffices, so tests/fakes needs no change.

claim: The client's cut of a refusal is checked only as "at most 300", so a text of exactly 300 characters can lose its last character to "…" (mutmut_25) and a longer one can be cut to 299 (mutmut_29).
evidence: tests/unit/test_erpnext.py::test_a_refusal_is_at_most_300_characters (line 248) asserts only `len(text) <= 300`; tests/integration/test_master_data.py::test_a_long_erpnext_message_reaches_the_agent_cut_to_300 adds only the prefix. The exact boundary is pinned for the tool layer's cut in tests/unit/test_tools.py::test_a_refusal_of_300_is_kept_whole_and_one_of_301_is_cut_to_300 ("REQ-001-PRS-F008: only a text over 300 characters is cut, to exactly 300"), but that test raises a Refusal directly and never reaches Erpnext._refusal (src/enterich/erpnext.py:248-249). Both mutants stay within the spec's 300 characters, so this is the code's contract rather than a spec breach. The client's cut is the only one applied to the ERPNext text inside a failed comment's warning (src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:131-132). Checked on scratch copies: a boundary test passes on the original and fails on each mutant.
proposal: Add a test in tests/unit/test_erpnext.py using the `failure` helper: with prefix "ERPNext refused the request (417 ValidationError). ERPNext's message: ", a message that fills the text to exactly 300 characters comes back whole, and one character more comes back as the first 299 characters plus "…" (length 300).

verdict.reason:
I couldn't refute it. The cut is at src/enterich/erpnext.py:248-249 (`if len(text) > MAX_MESSAGE: text = text[: MAX_MESSAGE - 1] + "…"`). `mutmut show` reports both mutants as survived: _refusal__mutmut_25 changes `>` to `>=`, and _refusal__mutmut_29 changes the slice to `MAX_MESSAGE - 2`.

No test asserts the boundary. I searched all of tests/, including tests/e2e. The client's cut is checked only as an upper bound, at 2,000 characters: tests/unit/test_erpnext.py:248-250 (`len(text) <= 300`) and tests/integration/test_master_data.py:282-289 (prefix plus `<= 300`). The only exact check is tests/unit/test_tools.py:102-116, which raises `tools.Refusal` directly and so exercises only `_refused` (src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:321-324), never `Erpnext._refusal`. No other test contains "…", and no test checks the text of the comment-failure warning.

Neither mutant is equivalent, and the agent sees the difference. The tool layer's second cut leaves a text of 300 or fewer characters alone (src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:304, 322), so the client's cut decides what an ERPNext refusal looks like. It is also the only cut on the ERPNext text inside the comment warning (src/enterich/tools/__init__.py:132).

I ran a throwaway test on scratch copies of src/enterich, outside the repository, using the `failure` helper with the prefix "ERPNext refused the request (417 ValidationError). ERPNext's message: ". A text of exactly 300 characters must come back whole, and one of 301 must come back as the first 299 characters plus "…". It passes on the original. The 300 case fails on mutant 25 (last character replaced by "…"), and the 301 case fails on mutant 29 (298 characters plus "…").

On whether the behaviour is required: REQ-001-PRS-F008 (docs/specs/req-001-core.md:296, DoD line 306) says the error carries ERPNext's first message and is at most 300 characters. Mutant 25 alters a message that fits the limit, which nothing in the spec permits. Mutant 29 stays within the spec's wording, and one boundary test covers both.

An earlier run (harness/runs/2026-11-12-tests-2/findings.jsonl) refuted this same finding as "not required" and said the same reasoning applied to `_refused`. I depart from that verdict because the twin finding for `_refused` was confirmed in that run and its test is on main (commit 1e0493c), with the docstring "REQ-001-PRS-F008: only a text over 300 characters is cut, to exactly 300". harness/suppressions.jsonl is empty, so the earlier drop isn't binding.

The fix is one test in tests/unit/test_erpnext.py with the existing `failure` helper. It needs no change to code, specs or ADRs. The limit is tested at 2,000 and never at 300 and 301, which is the limit-not-at-boundary class.
